text: Long ago, under a different name, Adolph Myers, Wing Biddlebaum had been a teacher in a small town in Pennsylvania, where the boys of his school loved him. <break time="0.8s" /> He was one of those rare men who are meant by nature to teach the young, and he ruled his pupils not by force but by a gentle power. <break time="0.8s" /> In the evening he walked with the boys or sat talking with them on the schoolhouse steps, and his voice became soft and musical as he spoke. <break time="0.8s" /> His hands moved as he talked, patting the boys shoulders now and then, for through his hands he tried to put his dreams into their young minds. <break time="0.8s" /> Under that gentle touch, doubt and disbelief went out of the boys, and they too began to dream, which was exactly what their teacher had hoped for. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a confused boy of the school misunderstood his teachers kindness and told a strange, untrue story about him as if it were a fact. <break time="0.8s" /> The parents believed the story, and the gentle touch that had come from his care for the boys was now seen as something to fear. <break time="0.8s" /> One dark, rainy night a crowd of angry men came to his house with lanterns, and they drove him out of town into the darkness.
